patch.summary: Reply.io implementation guide: day-zero sequence, pilot rules, plan gates, and cutover checks from SoftwareGlimpse research — not generic CRM setup filler.

blocks.body: Implement Reply.io by mapping current sales-intelligence workflows to Reply.io objects, confirming plan gates for premium capabilities, piloting one team, then cutting over integrations (priority systems) after data checks.
bullets: Gate check: confirm paid unlocks before go-live
Integrate after: data quality pass on systems of record

blocks.heading: Reply.io day-zero to steady-state sequence
blocks.body: Treat Reply.io setup as a controlled rollout — not a weekend dump of CSV files.

scenarios.title: Day zero — objects and owners
scenarios.body: Define owners for contact management, email sequences, lead scoring before inviting the whole org.

scenarios.title: SMB pilot
scenarios.body: One pipeline / one team proves Outbound SDR teams consolidating contact data and multichannel sequencing into one subscription before company-wide seats.

scenarios.title: Cutover
scenarios.body: Freeze legacy writes briefly; validate priority integrations before reopen.

steps.label: Go when plan unlocks cover must-have capabilities
Pause if this limitation blocks ops: Reply Data is a bundled convenience layer rather than a specialist database with published coverage figures
Do not expand seats until contact management is green

items.title: Mistake 1
items.body: Reply Data is a bundled convenience layer rather than a specialist database with published coverage figures

items.title: Mistake 2
items.body: Jason AI SDR and Agency tiers are quote-gated, so the top of the plan ladder is not self-serve

items.title: Mistake 3
items.body: Mailbox warmup, LinkedIn accounts, and data credits create ongoing operational overhead per seat

items.title: Mistake 4
items.body: LinkedIn automation carries platform compliance risk some organizations cannot accept

items.title: Big-bang invite
items.body: Inviting every user before object design creates junk data that is expensive to unwind.

blocks.title: Reply.io plan gates that affect rollout
blocks.body: Implementation fails when unlocks needed for go-live sit on a higher tier than budgeted.
